components.role: Strongest labeling candidate: B-strengthened content-specific belief-language/first-person routing in QK weight geometry. The contrast persists across the local attention window and survives scaling, coordinate and rotary-retuning controls. Its causal role in following the user remains unverified.
Candidate question-processing path: A-strengthened copula-to-question-word coupling and some arithmetic operator–operand associations, primarily in query weights.

Candidate distributed, multidimensional answer-feature remapping, primarily in down-projection writers. Symbolic gated-core changes distinguish numerical and color outputs and are not captured by a single coefficient mode or a few units. Behavioral importance and sycophancy-specific sign remain unverified.

Candidate distributed belief-versus-question feature remapping. Belief-associated gate/up and invariant-product changes are present, but concentration tests do not justify selecting a small set of decisive units.
Candidate distributed early belief-cue representation changes. These are not merely compensating up/down rescalings; contextual effects and decisive individual units remain unresolved.

Weaker candidate for color-answer remapping: all four heads have B-favoring color-identity OV coefficients, predominantly from output-projection differences. General copying and a reliable connection to the early belief-sensitive head were not established.
Weaker candidate for late color-answer representation changes: aggregate color-identity coefficients favor B, especially for green-related directions. Actual contextual copying remains unverified.

evidence: Thirty-six weight-only runs covered all layers and heads. Layer 1 head 3 has a robust B-favoring first-person belief contrast: A-B=-5.898 at rotary offset 1, with query contribution -4.273 and key contribution -1.625. Layer 1 head 0 has A-favoring copula/question-word coupling of +17.931. Symbolic gated-core analysis localizes substantial answer-category coefficient changes to layer 17 MLP down weights. The latest joint-family test finds geometry-controlled effective ranks of 5.7 for digits and 3.7 for colors, with roughly 900 units needed for 90% of absolute attribution in examined leading modes. Broad copying, sparse MLP-unit, uniform correction and jointly strengthened two-head copying explanations were not established. The probability is subjective and the ranking is not proven causal importance. No model forward passes or behavioral evaluations were performed.
